scripts/e2e-selection-actions.mjs.quarantineReason: 2026-08-17: harness debt, source-proven, not a product defect. The journey was written on 2026-08-11 (981e8ffd) and no suite, npm script or workflow ever selected it, so nothing noticed when 3d79497f "fix(outliner): add OG-compatible nested block drops" (2026-08-12, GH #326) landed one day later. That change added blockDropPosition(), which returns "child" whenever clientX - blockRect.left > 50 -- OG's deeper-than-50px nesting zone. This journey drops at target.left + width * 0.65, far beyond 50px, so B+C are now nested under E and the visible roots are A,D,E rather than A,D,E,B,C. Failed identically on two unchanged-binary runs at 4253d52b (72.3s, 72.0s; capsule step "drag B+C from A bullet to after E"). The drop x-coordinate is explicitly a nonRequirement of this very contract, so the repair belongs to the harness, not the product: aim the drop inside E's shallow (<= 50px from its left edge) zone and keep the vertical half that means "after". Quarantined under the AGENTS.md 2b E2E stop-loss after two attempts instead of debugging further; it stays selected by linux-release so its evidence is retained, and returns to stable with that coordinate repair.

scripts/e2e-dirty-editor-replacement.mjs.notes: GH #304, fixed in GH #254 increment 3. Two files legitimately share one page name (the duplicate-day stray of #21, or same-titled pages in different folders). Replacing the loaded instance destroyed the unsaved edit, and the dirty mark SURVIVED to describe the replacement's content, so the next save wrote the wrong file's bytes under the user's intent. The journey deliberately continues past 'the edit survived' to prove the refusal is not a trap: a survival-only assertion would pass on an implementation that never shows the requested file at all, which is why the non-wedging half is blocking rather than advisory. QUARANTINED 2026-08-10, harness debt. The first two assertions run green against the branch binary — the unsaved edit survives — but the journey drives the second file through an invented `#/page-path/...` hash route that the router does not implement, so the navigation never happens and the survival assertion passes VACUOUSLY. It is quarantined rather than deleted because the journey shape is right; what is missing is a real UI affordance for opening a same-named file by path (the duplicate-day journal conflicts list is the honest candidate). ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE 2026-08-10: no user gesture opens a chosen file by path. The router does support a path-pinned route (Page.tsx uses r.path -> getPageByPath), and the Quick Switcher is the only UI carrying a per-file path into openFile, but its row renders kind and name ONLY (QuickSwitcher.tsx Row), so two files sharing a page name are visually identical and a user cannot choose between them; selecting positionally would be exactly the brittle oracle the semantic-E2E contract forbids. No duplicates/conflicts list exists, and the router is not exposed on window, so browser.execute cannot reach openFile without adding a production test hook. The journey stays quarantined until such an affordance exists - which is itself the product gap GH #304's scenario implies. Until then the composition-level regressions in src/instanceReplacement.test.ts carry this contract; they drive the real store and both fail against the pre-fix code.

contracts.authority: GH #254 increment 2, conflict-override authority: an override is bound to the exact bytes the user was shown. Discarding an unseen external write is irrecoverable loss of another writer's work.

When that click is refused, a live banner returns for the conflict the user now actually has, so they are never left holding an unsaved edit with nothing to act on.

acceptableVariations: Banner wording, styling, and whether it re-renders in place or is replaced.

scripts/e2e-conflict-keep-mine.mjs.notes: GH #254. This is the sequence increment 2's adversarial rounds 3 and 4 each found broken in different places, and which nothing outside a mocked backend has ever driven. The failure is silent: "Keep mine" appears to work, and what is lost is someone else's write that the user cannot see was ever there. The non-wedging half is blocking because a refusal that leaves no live banner strands the edit — a conflicted page is skipped by the ordinary save path, so the user has no route back. QUARANTINED 2026-08-10, harness debt, NOT a product defect. Run against the branch binary it reproducibly showed "Keep mine" overwriting the second external winner. That is increment 2's DESIGNED outcome for this timing: a conflicted page is skipped by the ordinary save path, so the only thing that mints authority for a newer winner is the watcher's re-observation — and once that runs, the banner is re-armed and the click legitimately answers the CURRENT conflict. The harm the contract actually forbids is answering with authority minted for a DIFFERENT winner, i.e. a click that RACES the re-observation, which this journey does not construct: it waits 8s first. Fixing it means driving the stale-click shape (issue the force while a re-observation is in flight), which needs a deterministic hook the harness does not have. gh254_a_second_force_under_one_banner_cannot_spend_authority_for_an_unseen_winner covers that shape at the core boundary meanwhile.
